requirement: Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Inputs MUST be grouped under headings in this order, each input appearing once, in the first group that applies to it: Implementation, for sources reached by an `{impl}` edge from the definition, including anchored files; Tests, for sources reached by a `{test}` edge, including tests, examples, and anchored files; Referenced definitions, for declarations the definition cites and their terminology; and Other sources, for the remaining inputs the assessment consulted. Edges MUST be determined from the current references under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Each group and each input MUST be a collapsible disclosure element, with groups expanded and inputs collapsed by default, so readers can move between groups and open individual sources. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. An outline input MUST show its file, selector, kind, and current inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each outline input subsection MUST show the node's current source text in a fenced code block and say when its hash no longer matches; a requirements or definition input subsection MUST show its recorded text. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
rationale:
**Judgment: `requirements.index.detail_format` is satisfied.** Every obligation has marked implementation code and test coverage. I found two small marking gaps, which I judged non-blocking. **Implementation** (all in `src/index.rs` unless noted) - **State badge.** `render_detail_sections` calls `shield_badge` (`src/lib.rs`). It builds a static `img.shields.io/badge/evidence--` image with alt text such as `evidence Valid`. - **Body block quote.** `render_detail_sections` writes a `## Requirement` or `## Example` heading, labeled by kind. It then writes the current definition text, passed from `render_detail_page`, as `> ` block-quote lines. It does not use the recorded text. - **Rationale and FIXME.** The rationale is pushed raw under `## Rationale` so it renders as Markdown, with a placeholder when none is recorded. Recorded FIXME strings come from `Judgment::fixme_entries` (`src/judgment.rs`), pass through `LoadedDetailEvidence::fixme_entries` and `borrowed`, and are shown under `## FIXME references`. - **Grouping.** `InputGroup` and its `heading` and `id` give the order Implementation, Tests, Referenced definitions, Other sources. `DefinitionEdges::current` collects the current `{impl}` and `{test}` reference sites and the `{cite}` names in the definition text. It also resolves `:impl:` and `:test:` anchors to their current line ranges. `DefinitionEdges::group` returns the first group that applies: a reference site or anchor overlapping the input's ranges, then a definition input or a fully cited requirements input, otherwise Other sources. Each input is therefore placed once, in the first applicable group. - **Disclosure elements.** Groups are `
` and inputs are `
`, which is collapsed by default. - **Input subsections.** Each input has a `` that names its selector (`render_input`). An outline input shows File, Selector, Kind and the inclusive `file:start–end` range. A requirements or definition input shows each match as `name: file:start–end` (`render_source_location`, using `SourceRange` from `src/inputs.rs`). - **Source text and staleness.** An outline input shows its current text in a fenced block and adds a "recorded hash no longer matches" notice when the hash differs. A requirements or definition input shows its recorded `text`. `push_code_block` lengthens the fence when the text contains backticks. - **Highlighting.** `code_language` maps `rs` to `rust,noplayground`, `toml` to `ini`, and the Markdown, JSON, Java, JS, TS and Python extensions to their language names. Recorded requirement text uses the Markdown fence. **Tests** - `detail_page_renders_markdown_and_highlighted_input_sections` checks: - the badge and the block quote with a nested heading; - Markdown rationale; - the outline input summary, File/Selector/Kind/range lines, the Rust fence and the stale-hash notice (exactly once); - the whole-file Markdown fence with its backtick-lengthened fence, and the TOML-as-ini fence. - `common_input_extensions_select_highlighting_languages` covers every language mapping, plus the plaintext fallback. - `detail_inputs_are_grouped_by_current_edges_in_disclosures` checks: - group order and the placement of each input: an impl reference site, an impl anchor, a test site, an example test edge, a cited requirement, and Other sources; - 4 open groups, 7 inputs and 11 `
` tags. - `detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group` checks: - the alt text `evidence Invalid`; - match name and range lines followed by the recorded text; - definition inputs and unresolved selectors; - a dual impl+test source appearing once, under Implementation only. - `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` (`tests/outcomes.rs`) checks the FIXME badge, the `## FIXME references` heading and the FIXME entries on a detail page. `index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages` checks the Example label and the missing-evidence placeholder. **Minor observations (not blocking)** - `DetailEvidence` is marked only `{cite}`, but it is a plain carrier struct. The behavior it carries is implemented in the marked `borrowed` and `render_detail_sections`. - The `InputGroup::ALL` const, which fixes the display order, has no marker of its own. The `InputGroup` enum and its `heading` and `id` carry `{impl}` markers. - The only anchor kind tested for grouping is `:impl:`. The `:test:` path is the same code, so I treated that as acceptable.

text: :::{req} detail_format

Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Inputs MUST be grouped under headings in this order, each input appearing once, in the first group that applies to it: Implementation, for sources reached by an `{impl}` edge from the definition, including anchored files; Tests, for sources reached by a `{test}` edge, including tests, examples, and anchored files; Referenced definitions, for declarations the definition cites and their terminology; and Other sources, for the remaining inputs the assessment consulted. Edges MUST be determined from the current references under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Each group and each input MUST be a collapsible disclosure element, with groups expanded and inputs collapsed by default, so readers can move between groups and open individual sources. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. An outline input MUST show its file, selector, kind, and current inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each outline input subsection MUST show the node's current source text in a fenced code block and say when its hash no longer matches; a requirements or definition input subsection MUST show its recorded text. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references: discovery MUST skip `.git` and `target` directories at any depth and the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.targets`
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`
{test}`requirements.references.targets`
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
